traits.leaf_incision.note: German Wikipedia, Nelkengewächse (read 2026-10-17): blades undivided and entire. DELTA, Caryophyllaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina entire, simple.

traits.leaf_shape.note: German Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17): family leaves elongate (Nelkengewächse); Silene, the largest genus, awl-shaped, linear, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate or elliptic (Leimkräuter); Dianthus narrow, linear, lanceolate to ovate (Nelken); English Wikipedia, Dianthus: mostly linear. Weighted by Silene then Dianthus.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 1-10 in 1 or 2 whorls; FOC (2-)5-10. Agrees with the family file.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Flora of China vol. 6 (2001), Caryophyllaceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves opposite, decussate (successive pairs crossing). Confirms the family file.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals persistent in fruit, (3-)4-5; petals (1-)4-5. FOC: sepals and petals (4 or) 5. Adds the rare 3 as low.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): styles 1-5(-6) and stigmas 2-5(-6); FOC carpels 2-5 united into one ovary. The rare 6 added as high.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 374: corolla of 5 free, often clawed petals. Free petals: rotate by PlantGen's free-petal rule; the book names no other corolla form. (The claws sit inside the calyx tube, so the spread limbs can read as salverform.)

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 374, 378: hypanthium absent, rarely present; formula 'hypanthium usually absent'.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 273 Caryophyllaceae: annual or perennial herbs; leaves opposite, simple, entire, often joined at the base by a line across the stem; stipules absent, or papery where present; flowers regular, mostly bisexual, alone or in cymes; sepals free or joined in a tube; petals as many as the sepals, often small or absent; up to 10 stamens; ovary superior with its ovules on a free central column; fruit a dry capsule opening by valves or teeth at the top. The few species with papery stipules (the sandworts' kin) are read as exceptions to 'stipules absent'. Library 1.0's family is 27% dwarf shrubs, stated as semi-woody sometimes.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): winter annual, annual, biennial or perennial; FOC annual or perennial. Agrees with the family file.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves opposite, pseudoverticillate or whorled, rarely alternate, often joined at the base. FOC: opposite and decussate, rarely alternate or verticillate. The family file's plain 'opposite' is kept as the usual state; whorls and alternate leaves added as rare.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves simple.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade margins entire; FOC: simple, entire.

traits.stipules.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stipules present or absent; the key and discussion tie stipules to subfamilies Polycarpoideae and Paronychioideae (genera 1-13 of 37 in the flora: Paronychia, Herniaria, Spergularia, Spergula, Drymaria and kin), absent in Alsinoideae and Caryophylloideae. FOC: stipules scarious, bristly, or often absent. So 'usually absent, sometimes present'.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers radially symmetric; FOC actinomorphic.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals (3-)4-5 and petals absent or (1-)4-5, often clawed: a calyx and corolla where petals are present.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): ovary 1, superior.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits capsules opening by valves or teeth, or a usually indehiscent utricle (Paronychioideae: Paronychia, Herniaria, Scleranthus and kin). FOC: usually a capsule, rarely berrylike or an achene. A one-seeded utricle that stays shut is read as an achene, rarely.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals persistent in fruit; FOC: sepals persistent.

traits.perianth_fused.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals distinct (free), often clawed; FOC petals free. The calyx can be a joined tube but the corolla is not.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): herbs (small trees, shrubs or vines outside the flora), stems herbaceous, sometimes from a woody caudex. FOC: herbs, rarely subshrubs or shrubs. Agrees with the family file.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescences terminal or axillary cymes, thyrses or capitula, or flowers solitary; FOC cymes or cymose panicles, rarely solitary or in racemes, capitula, umbels. Heads added as rare (Dianthus-like capitula).

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Caryophyllaceae family account (Rabeler & Hartman) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers bisexual or occasionally unisexual; Silene's account adds plants with pistillate flowers beside bisexual ones and rare dioecy. FOC: male-sterile flowers frequent in otherwise hermaphroditic Silene.
